thread.title: How Apple, Growth Stock Plays Are Holding Up During Correction

author: NANCY GONDO
title: How Apple, Growth Stock Plays Are Holding Up During Correction
text:
Growth stocks have gotten slapped down during the market correction as sector rotation occurred. So, how have growth-stock exchange traded funds fared?
X As you'd imagine, most endured a pretty tough month with losses ranging from 8.1% to 13.5%.
Despite the sharp losses, their year-to-date gains remain ahead of the broader market. Invesco Russell MidCap Pure Growth ( PXMG ) came in first with a 12.2% return, well ahead of the S&P 500's 3% year-to-date advance. The $245 million fund, which tracks the Russell Midcap Pure Growth Index, stumbled 13% in the past month.
PXMG outpaces the S&P 500 over the longer haul, with a three-year average annual return of 16% vs. the S&P's 11.5% gain, according to Morningstar Direct. Their five-year returns are nearly even: 11.7% for the ETF and 11.3% for the S&P 500.
Information technology accounted for the biggest sector weighting as of Wednesday, at about 43% of assets. Consumer discretionary was next at 21%, health care 14.5% and industrials 11%. Smaller positions in financials, communication services and materials made up the rest. Top five holdings — which included Square ( SQ ), Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) and Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ) — represented nearly 13% of the 97-stock portfolio.
Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) came in second with a 9.6% year-to-date gain. The $67.7 billion fund fell 8.6% during the past month. Its average annual return beats the S&P 500 for the past three years and five years at 15.5% and 16.7%, respectively. QQQ is based on the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 index.
Growth Stock: Apple Earnings Information technology represented 44% of assets, communication services 23%, consumer discretionary 16% and health care 9%. Consumer staples and industrials made up a respective 6% and 2%. The top five holdings — Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet ( GOOG ) and Facebook ( FB ) — accounted for about 43% of the portfolio.
Apple fell Thursday after the close, following its fiscal Q4 earnings report . The iPhone maker earned $2.91 a share on $62.9 billion in revenue, topping views for $2.78 a share on $61.6 billion in sales. But its revenue guidance for the current quarter disappointed. The stock reclaimed its 50-day moving average during the regular session Thursday.

It gave up 8.6% the past month. The $349.4 million fund, which tracks the Pacer Nasdaq 100 Trendpilot Index, launched in June 2015. Its three-year average annual return is 11.2%. PTNQ has the ability to pare back market exposure during short-term market declines and can move to Treasury bills during long-term downtrends.
As of Thursday, half its assets were in cash and "other." The top five holdings, which are the same as QQQ, made up 21% of assets.
